newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan industry output down 0.5 pct vs Dec.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan industry output down 0.5 pct vs Dec.

text.p: Output by Brazilian industry fell 0.5 percent in January over December but grew 6.7 percent when compared with January 1996, the National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said in a statement.
The cumulative index of the last twelve months also rose to 2.7 percent against 1.5 percent in December, it added.

Some 11 of the 20 sectors covered in the survey showed decreases in output in the last month over December, led by the clothing and material industry (down by 7.7 percent), the mechanical and metallurgical sectors (both down by 2.7 percent) and mineral extraction (down 2.1 percent).
Production of consumer durable goods rose 7.7 percent over December but semi-durable and non-durables, capital and intermediary goods all registered falls.
In the year-on-year result, 16 sectors showed gains, in particular the tobacco industry which rose 26.6 percent and electrical and communication materials (up 17.5 percent).
The greatest falls were seen in the clothing industry where output fell seven percent and food, down 6.7 percent.

Consumer durable goods showed an improvement of 24.5 percent last month over January 1996, with radio and sound equipment up 36.8 percent, cars up 18.7 percent and domestic electrical goods up 23.3 percent. ((-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
